items.title: November 13, 2026
items.summary: BigQueryFeatureBigQuery connections to MySQL,Oracle, andPostgreSQL are now available and can beused to run MySQL federated queries,Oracle federated queries, andPostgreSQL federated queries.These features are in Preview.BigtableFeatureYou can use the Google Cloud console to view and analyze read and write accesspatterns for your Bigtable instances and clusters, including request volume,latency, bandwidth, and row scan metrics broken down by query type. This featureis generally available (GA).For more information, seeAnalyze access patterns.Cloud SQL for MySQLFeatureCloud SQL enhanced backups support instances with disaster recovery (DR)replica instances. You can associate a Backup and DR backup plan directly with aprimary instance that has a designated DR replica.For more information, see Choose your backupoption andManage enhancedbackups.Cloud SQL for PostgreSQLFeatureCloud SQL enhanced backups support instances with disaster recovery (DR)replica instances. You can associate a Backup and DR backup plan directly with aprimary instance that has a designated DR replica.For more information, see Choose your backupoption andManage enhancedbackups.Cloud SQL for SQL ServerFeatureCloud SQL enhanced backups support instances with disaster recovery (DR)replica instances. You can associate a Backup and DR backup plan directly with aprimary instance that has a designated DR replica.For more information, see Choose your backupoption andManage enhancedbackups.Managed Service for Apache AirflowBreaking(Airflow 3.3.1, 3.2.2, and 2.11.1) Upgraded the pip package from version23.2.1 to version 26.2.2. This update is available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3)builds composer-3-airflow-3.3.1-build.8,composer-3-airflow-3.2.2-build.12, and composer-3-airflow-2.11.1-build.25and later, and in the Managed Airflow (Gen 2) imagecomposer-2.18.0-airflow-2.11.1 and later.This version includes security fixes and changes how custom PyPI packages areinstalled:PEP 440 version specifiers: pip 26.2.2 enforcesPEP 440 complianceand supports the .* wildcard only with == and !=. For example, usegcsfs>=0.8 instead of gcsfs>=0.8.*.Isolated source builds: source packages (.tar.gz) are always built inan isolated environment. If you install source packages from a privaterepository that is your only package index, make sure that the repositorycontains precompiled wheel packages (.whl) for setuptools and any otherbuild dependencies (listed under [build-system] requires inpyproject.toml). Alternatively, publish your packages as .whl packages.As a temporary workaround to disable build isolation, addno-build-isolation = false to the [global] section of your pip.conffile. This workaround works only if the build dependencies are alreadyinstalled in your environment.Legacy pkg_resources builds: older source packages that rely onpkg_resources might fail to build. Use newer package versions withprecompiled .whl packages, or for your own private packages, build themas .whl packages or update their build scripts so that they don't use thelegacy pkg_resources module.Make sure that your custom PyPI packages are compatible with these changesbefore you upgrade your environment. If the installation of PyPI packages failsduring an upgrade, your environment keeps running with its current version andpackages.
